strengths: Small object detection is a significant topic in the community of remote sensing image processing.
The research topic is significant and the authors explore and improve DETR-based detection, achieving an accuracy higher than several well-known methods.
The structure of this article is well-organized, including essential sections such as methodology and experiments. Additionally, the experimental setup is fairly reasonable.
Investigating a better DETR-like method for small object detection in remote sensing images is meaningful and challenging.
weaknesses: The authors state technical designs without appropriate citations, reusing ideas that have been proposed in existing works.

If the main work of this paper is utilizing some existing technologies to solve the remote sensing object detection problem, the authors should clarify this fact and provide appropriate citations; it is hard to judge the real contributions of the paper in its current organization.
A large part of this paper is plagiarised from papers [a] and [b] (arxiv version).
This paper's section 3.2 is plagiarised from both [a] and [b]. Specifically, L275-L286 is plagiarised from the section 3.3 of [b]. L287-L299 is plagiarised from the section 4.4 of [a].
This paper's section 3.3 is plagiarised from section 3.5 of [b].
This paper's Fig.1 is actually the Fig.1 of [b].
This paper's Fig.3 is actually the Fig.3 of [b].
There is no mention or citation to [a] and [b].
The related work is not comprehensive, e.g., a highly related work DINO [1] is not analyzed and compared.

The overall writing quality needs improvement. There are some errors, e.g., in Line 405 "TS TS-Deformable DETR". The caption of Fig. 1 is in lowercase, and the captions of other figures do not provide enough information.
The improvement calculation is misleading, e.g., in Line 491, "the AP is improved by 50.7%". Since AP is already a percentage value, a better way is 50.5% - 33.5% = 17.0%.

The article lacks innovation. Proposal Generation, Group Denoising, and Query Cascade Refinement have all been widely studied in works such as DINO, DAB-DETR, and Group DETR, yet the authors did not introduce any effective improvements and do not reference these previous works.

The comparative methods in the experiments are outdated, making it difficult to strongly validate the approach's effectiveness; the authors also did not compare their model with detection models like QueryDet that are specifically designed for small object detection tasks.

The experiments are severely insufficient. The authors only provided a table for the ablation study without further quantitative and qualitative analysis, such as visualizing detection results or the impact of the DeNoising module on the loss function.
The novelty of the proposed method is questionable, as it closely resembles DINO[1].

I did not find innovative designs compared to DINO. Since no supplementary material was submitted, anonymized code is necessary to verify these claims. Additionally, the paper does not cite DINO [1] or compare with it.
The `QPG` module (Query Proposal Generation) is similar to the `Mixed Query Selection` module of DINO[1].
Figure 2 is also similar to Figure 5(c) of DINO[1] paper.
The Group Denoising module is similar to the `Contrastive DeNoising Training` module of DINO[1].
Figure 3 is also similar to Figure 3 of DINO[1] paper.
The QCR module (Query Cascade Refinement) is similar to the `Look Forward Twice` module of DINO[1].
Formula 2 of this paper is similar to Formula 2 of DINO[1] paper.
The quality of the writing needs improvement, with several long paragraphs and repeated content.
The relevance of the proposed method to 'remote sensing images' and 'small object detection,' as stated in the title, is weak; the method appears to be intended for general object detection.

I disagree with the authors' claim that adopting a denoising strategy improves the model's robustness to feature noise caused by complex backgrounds in remote sensing images; the denoising is not used for inference.
